summary: A 1934 CCC-built 55-ft Aermotor fire tower on Stratton Mountain, Vermont, on the Appalachian Trail; fire spotting ended in 1982 and it is now open to climbers.

facts.design: 55-ft Aermotor steel tower with 7x7-ft cab (register and Green Mountain Club shelter history); USFS calls the renovated tower 70 ft

staffing.status: Green Mountain Club caretaker at the summit in summer and fall; fire spotting ended 1982

access.note: USFS says visitors may climb the renovated tower; the summit lies on the Appalachian and Long Trails. Current tower condition and any climbing rules were not verified on site.

visit.trail_note: White-blazed Appalachian and Long Trail from a parking area; about 1.4 miles to a forest road crossing, then the steeper climb to the summit.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Green Mountain National Forest)

events.note: Built by the Stratton Mountain Club with the Vermont State Forester; 60-ft steel tower per register and Green Mountain Club shelter history, 65-ft per nomination
Partly destroyed in a winter storm in 1920-21; remains continued in service
Watchman's cabin; nomination says probably built by sawmill owner Leon Stocker, GMC shelter history says built by the Vermont Timber Owners' Association and state forestry department
CCC built the present 55-ft Aermotor tower with 7x7-ft cab
State of Vermont built a larger prefabricated log cabin on the summit
Fire spotting ended after the 1982 season; one of the last three Vermont towers used for fire spotting
Forest Service acquired a large tract including the south summit (nomination)
Tower repaired and painted to serve for recreational viewing
Log cabin reopened to provide quarters for a resident
Register says the land and tower were purchased by the USFS in 1990
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1992

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the Green Mountain Club's shelter history give 60 ft. The nomination says 65 ft. The story reports both.

The register, the Green Mountain Club's shelter history and the nomination (about 55 ft above ground) give 55 ft. The USFS page calls the recently renovated tower 70 ft. The record keeps 55 ft (16.8 m); the 70 ft figure may reflect the renovation or a different measure, and an editor should check it.
The nomination says the Forest Service acquired a tract including the south summit in 1986. The register says the land and tower were purchased in 1990. The story reports both.

The nomination says Leon Stocker, a sawmill owner, probably built it, and the Timberland Owners Association arranged it. The Green Mountain Club's shelter history credits the Timber Owners' Association and the state forestry department. These read as consistent: the association arranged the work and Stocker built it.

notes_for_editor: Several sources disagree on dates and heights (see resolved_conflicts). The 'today' access rests on an undated USFS trail page. The NRHP nomination is dated March 1990 (Hugh H. Henry), before the 1992 listing. A Stratton Mountain Resort hiking page (search snippet only, not fetched; the fetch returned no text) says the tower was manned until 1979, which conflicts with the nomination's 1982; it is not cited and remains unverified. No rental listing found; the cabin is a Green Mountain Club shelter, not described as rentable. The NRHP ID 92000687 and the 1992 listing are from the brief and the NPGallery detail page; the listing year is from the GMC page. Consider updating facts.height_m if the USFS 70 ft figure is confirmed for the renovated tower.
